items.title: Turkije profiteert niet van historische rode kaart Almirón en is uitgeschakeld
items.summary: Het WK is op een grote mislukking uitgedraaid voor Turkije. Omdat de ploeg van coach Vincenzo Montella in San Francisco niet kon winnen van een tiental van Paraguay, zijn de Turken al uitgeschakeld. En dat is niet de enige reden dat het treffen de geschiedenisboeken ingaat. items.title: Toen Zlatan tijdens Zweden-Nederland zijn Ajax-maatje Raffa torpedeerde
items.summary: In de rubriek VI Tijdmachine brengen we met regelmaat nieuwe verhalen over toen, en elke dag van het weekeinde herplaatsen we een artikel uit ons rijke archief. Deze keer gaan we in aanloop naar Nederland-Zweden 22 jaar terug in de tijd, naar een eerder duel tussen beide landen. Als Zlatan Ibrahimovic zijn Ajax-maatje Rafael van der Vaart compleet de vernieling in schopt. Een reconstructie van een aantal krankzinnige maanden rond de zomerse deadline day van 2004, met een prominente bijrol voor Ronald Koeman.

items.title: ‘That penalty changed my life’: Panenka’s pride 50 years on from special spot-kick
items.summary: Czech’s audacious defiance of Sepp Maier in Belgrade has slipped into football folklore: ‘The only disadvantage is that I don’t get any royalties from it’ Antonin Panenka laughs like a bear might, a low rumble, suggesting mischief among the memories. He is sat in an office at Bohemians football club in Prague, recounting the story of his impudent, revolutionary penalty that not only won the 1976 European Championship for Czechoslovakia against West Germany but soured his relationship with the goalkeeper his spot-kick humiliated, Sepp Maier. “He went 35 years without uttering a single word to me,” he smiles. But the feud went much deeper. “I read some articles that he even had a shooting target in his garage with my face on it that he used to fire darts at. We get on well enough now though.” Continue reading...

items.title: Brazil sweep into form as Cunha’s quickfire double sparks World Cup win over Haiti
items.summary: On a sticky, fun, occasionally boisterous, occasionally listless night in Philadelphia Brazil eased past a game but limited Haiti. All three goals in this 3-0 win came during a spell of first-half urgency driven by the high-grade wide play of Vinícius Júnior and Raphinha. In that period Brazil’s wide forwards were simply too much for a Haiti team that looked like it was trying to defend in a dogged low block, which gave the appearance of cautious, deep defence, but with the added key variation of also leaving huge open spaces in exactly the wrong places. Haiti, with no goals and no points, are now certain to finish bottom of Group C and face a final fixture against Morocco in Atlanta next week. There is also an oddity for Scotland now, who are likely to play their fixture against Brazil uncertain as to what result is required, needing to wait for the other groups to finish before knowing their destiny. Thanks, again, for that Gianni. Pile ‘em high. Deal with the consequences later. Continue reading...

items.title: Socceroos aggrieved by referee’s ‘stinker’ in World Cup defeat to USA
items.summary: German official Felix Zwayer faces criticism for perceived injustices Tony Popovic encouraged by much improved second-half performance Referee Felix Zwayer has come in for criticism from the Socceroos, who labelled the German’s performance a “stinker” after what they believed was a series of injustices in their 2-0 defeat to the USA in the World Cup match in Seattle. The co-hosts’ second goal was awarded by the video referee, and it was contentious given what appeared to be an offside player in the proximity of goalkeeper Patrick Beach when he tried to recover from a misdirected shot. items.title: Saibari strikes after 70 seconds as Morocco puncture Scotland’s World Cup party
items.summary: Scotland would have taken this outcome after 70 seconds. Ismael Saibiri had fired this highly-rated Moroccan team ahead. Men in kilts gulped under the blazing Massachusetts sun. Scotland may even privately have taken this outcome before a ball was kicked. Avoidance of a comprehensive defeat against Brazil will leave them with at least a fighting chance of becoming the first Scotland team to progress to the knockout phase of a major tournament. Easier said than done, of course, but a scenario where history remains within the grasp of Steve Clarke and his players. Onwards to Miami, for what promises to be quite the spectacle. The value in beating Haiti by a goal or only losing this by the same will all be apparent by full-time on Wednesday. The Tartan Army need calculators in hand. Continue reading...
